Question: A point is selected at random inside an equilateral triangle. From this point perpendiculars are dropped to each side. The sum of these perpendiculars is:

Choices.A:
Least when the point is the center of gravity of the
triangle
Choices.B: Greater than the altitude of the triangle
Choices.C: Equal to the altitude of the triangle
Choices.D: One-half the sum of the sides of the triangle
Choices.E: Greatest when the point is the center of gravity

Solution:
The equal side lengths suggest using each side as the base of a smaller triangle. Let the equilateral triangle have side length \(s>0\) and altitude \(h\). Let \(P\) be the selected interior point, and let \(d_1,d_2,d_3\) be its perpendicular distances to the three sides.

Join \(P\) to all three vertices. The resulting three triangles cover the original triangle and have no overlapping interiors. Each has base \(s\), and its corresponding height is one of the perpendicular distances. Adding their areas gives
\[
\frac12sd_1+\frac12sd_2+\frac12sd_3
=\frac12sh.
\]
Dividing by \(s/2>0\), we obtain
\[
d_1+d_2+d_3=h.
\]
Thus the sum is the same for every interior point, regardless of the random selection. It equals the triangle's altitude, choice C.
